source_task: CVIP2026 research-upgrade, final-validation pass (v2), building on Phases 1-10 (v1, dated 2026-08-12)

evidence_classification_key.REAL: Computed from isl_dataset.csv / isl_dataset_kaggle_controlled.csv as they exist today, by a script in this repo, reproducible.
evidence_classification_key.MANUAL: A true, factual finding from a one-time manual inspection outside the repo (not auto-reproducible).
evidence_classification_key.HYPOTHESIS: A plausible, evidence-motivated explanation NOT experimentally confirmed.
evidence_classification_key.TESTED_AND_REFUTED: A specific candidate cause that WAS experimentally tested and did not hold up -- reported as a negative result, not omitted.
evidence_classification_key.FUTURE_WORK: Designed/specified but not executed -- zero data exists for this.

dataset.signer_session_caveat: These are placeholder source tags (unknown_legacy / kaggle_unknown / unassigned_signer / kaggle_import / unassigned_session), not real signer or session identities. No signer-independent or session-independent claim is made anywhere in this evaluation.

kaggle_source.name: Indian Sign Language (ISL)
kaggle_source.author: prathumarikeri
kaggle_source.license_verified_by: user, 2026-08-12, from the Kaggle dataset page (usability 8.75)

image_resolution_heterogeneity.finding: 31/35 classes are uniformly 1200x 128x128px tightly-cropped hand photos; C/I/O/V additionally contain 90-247 extra images each from a different, much higher-resolution sub-source (640x480 or ~1088x1920), matching those same 4 classes' >1200-row counts in isl_dataset_kaggle.csv.
image_resolution_heterogeneity.status: well-evidenced fact; NOT experimentally confirmed as a cause of the cross-domain gap

near_duplication.caveat: burst_id is near-unique per row for the Kaggle-sourced majority of the data (mean group size ~1.03); this diagnostic is only informative for the small legacy-webcam subset that actually has multi-row bursts.

leakage_demo.interpretation: Unlike the pre-Kaggle-merge dataset (where burst-disjoint splitting collapsed accuracy to 0% because almost every class had exactly one burst), burst-disjoint and naive-random splits now give SIMILAR results. This is not because leakage was fixed -- it's because burst_id is near-unique per row for 97% of the current data (Kaggle-sourced), so grouping by burst barely constrains the split at all. burst_id is not a meaningful leakage control at the current dataset composition.

repeated_split_stats.pseudo_replication_caveat: The 10 seeds are overlapping 80/20 resamples of the same 31688 deduplicated rows, not 10 independent datasets -- this measures sensitivity to split randomness, not true sampling variability.

results.interpretation: in_domain_* results show what accuracy this feature representation/classifier achieves when train and test come from the same source. kaggle_to_webcam and webcam_to_kaggle show what happens when the model has never seen the OTHER source at all. A large drop from in-domain to cross-domain accuracy is evidence of genuine domain shift (capture device / lighting / temporal smoothing / detection-threshold differences), not of the model failing to learn the sign shapes themselves.

h3_feature_shift_within_class.method: within-class Cohen's d, averaged across classes (not a marginal/class-agnostic comparison)

h8_hand_proximity_test_INCONCLUSIVE.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE -- visually motivated (overlapping/close hands in E,F,K,M Kaggle images) but the quantitative inter-hand-distance test shows no clean separation between failing and succeeding classes. Do not report as a confirmed cause.

Do not report as a confirmed cause.

new_v2_experiment_1_confidence_controlle.description: Re-extracted the raw Kaggle images at MediaPipe confidence=0.7 (matching isl_main.py's live-app detection+presence thresholds exactly, up from the original importer's 0.5 default) via import_kaggle_dataset.py --confidence 0.7, then reran all 4 cross-source settings against this controlled extraction.

results.limitation_one_euro_filtering_not_contro: One-Euro temporal filtering (webcam) vs. none (Kaggle, static photos) could NOT be controlled for -- raw unfiltered webcam video frames were never saved, only the final filtered feature vectors. Retroactively removing the filter's effect, or fabricating an 'unfiltered webcam' dataset, is not possible without new data collection. This asymmetry is partly inherent to comparing a photo dataset against a video-capture dataset and is reported as an unresolved limitation, not a fixed confound.

new_v2_experiment_1_confidence_controlle.verdict: REFUTED as an explanation for the cross-source gap: controlling the confidence threshold does NOT close the gap. Kaggle-to-Webcam macro-F1 goes from 0.312 to 0.275 (WORSE, not better); Webcam-to-Kaggle from 0.211 to 0.202 (also worse). In-domain accuracy is essentially unchanged in both cases (+0.02pp Kaggle, +0.00pp webcam). The detection-confidence mismatch documented in the v1 dossier is NOT a driver of the domain-shift gap.

new_v2_experiment_2_handswap_hypothesis_.description: Tested whether a systematic right/left hand-column mislabeling between isl_main.py's deliberate MediaPipe-handedness-swap/un-mirror correction and the offline Kaggle importer's un-corrected raw MediaPipe label (surfaced during this pass's code audit, not previously tested) explains the still-unexplained two-handed failures (A, E, F). Swapped the right/left 63-column blocks for two-handed webcam test rows and re-evaluated the SAME Kaggle-trained raw-132 model.

results.hypothesis: Systematic right/left hand-column mislabeling between isl_main.py's un-mirror correction and import_kaggle_dataset.py's raw-MediaPipe-label convention explains some of the residual (H6-unexplained) cross-domain failures for two-handed classes.
results.method_caveat: Only the 126 raw per-landmark columns were swapped exactly; the 6 inter-hand relative-delta features (126:132) were left unchanged because their pre-normalization raw inputs are not recoverable from the stored, already-normalized CSV -- this under-tests the hypothesis for those 6 features only.
results.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED -- swapping hand blocks does not materially recover any previously-failing two-handed class. The un-mirror/handedness-swap convention mismatch is not shown to be a cause of the A/E/F/K residual failures by this test.

new_v2_experiment_2_handswap_hypothesis_.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED -- swapping hand blocks does not materially recover any previously-failing two-handed class. The un-mirror/handedness-swap convention mismatch is not shown to be a cause of the A/E/F/K residual failures by this test.

new_v2_experiment_3_landmark_geometry_vi._evidence: REAL (qualitative, visual, reconstructed directly from stored feature vectors, no original images needed)
new_v2_experiment_3_landmark_geometry_vi.finding: Visual comparison of reconstructed hand skeletons (Kaggle vs. webcam, 3 samples each) for A, E, F, K (unexplained failures) and G (working control). K's Kaggle samples are visibly and consistently TWO-handed while its webcam samples are visibly and consistently ONE-handed (right only) -- corroborating H6's aggregate stat (kaggle K: 94.7% both-hands, webcam K: 100% right-only) as an near-total hand-count mismatch, not just a compositional skew. This is a materially stronger explanation for K's failure than H6 alone conveyed: the classifier trained on two-handed Kaggle K samples has structurally never seen a one-handed K, in either raw or handslot-agnostic representations. A's Kaggle and webcam samples both show two hands but in visibly different postures (wide/spread vs. compact/vertical) -- visual support for genuine postural/framing divergence, still not causally isolated. E and F look visually SIMILAR in overall hand shape between domains despite still failing at 0% recall -- visual evidence AGAINST a simple whole-hand-shape explanation for those two specifically, sharpening (not resolving) the open question.

new_v2_experiment_4_classifier_generaliz.description: Hostile-ML-review question: every domain-shift forensic experiment used RandomForest only -- is the gap an RF artifact? Trained kNN(k=5), SVM-RBF(C=10), and MLP(128,64) on Kaggle (raw 132-d, shared classes), tested on Webcam, compared to RandomForest.

results.verdict: Cross-domain (Kaggle->Webcam) accuracy ranges 42.3%-50.6% and macro-F1 0.254-0.324 across RandomForest/kNN/SVM-RBF/MLP -- all four collapse far below their ~99%+ in-domain accuracy (evaluate.py section 6). The domain-shift gap is not a RandomForest-specific artifact; it holds, with some spread, across every classifier family tested.

new_v2_experiment_4_classifier_generaliz.verdict: Cross-domain (Kaggle->Webcam) accuracy ranges 42.3%-50.6% and macro-F1 0.254-0.324 across RandomForest/kNN/SVM-RBF/MLP -- all four collapse far below their ~99%+ in-domain accuracy (evaluate.py section 6). The domain-shift gap is not a RandomForest-specific artifact; it holds, with some spread, across every classifier family tested.

mcnemar_paired_significance_test.description: Paired McNemar exact test (raw_132 vs handslot_agnostic_41, same test rows) added this pass, since non-overlapping bootstrap CIs alone are a weaker significance claim than a paired test on the same predictions.
mcnemar_paired_significance_test.verdict: Both directions significant at p < 1e-9. The handslot-agnostic improvement is real, not noise.

multiseed_robustness_check.verdict: Handslot-agnostic's worst-case seed still beats raw's best-case seed on Kaggle->Webcam macro-F1 across 7 RandomForest seeds -- not a single-lucky-seed artifact.

candidate_fix_phase5.description: Hand-slot-agnostic rotation/reflection-invariant angle features (41-d) vs. raw (132-d)
candidate_fix_phase5.verdict: Statistically significant (non-overlapping 95% CIs, McNemar p<1e-9, seed-robust) partial improvement in both cross-domain directions; recovers U and M classes; A/E/F/J/K remain at 0% recall -- NOT a full fix. The hand-swap and confidence-control experiments this pass further show the residual A/E/F/K failures are not explained by the two most plausible remaining pipeline-level confounds either.

handedness_analysis.caveat: Handedness here is inferred from which hand-feature block is non-zero at capture time, not ground-truth sign linguistics (some classes are inherently one-handed signs; this mixes 'sign is one-handed' with 'only one hand was detected'). A single classifier trained on the full mixed-handedness training set is evaluated separately on each test subset, so this measures whether ONE model generalizes evenly across handedness conditions, not whether per-handedness specialist models would do better.

classifier_comparison.caveat: Held-out stratified 80/20 split (post-dedup). SVM-RBF trained on a stratified subsample capped at 6000 rows for tractability (RandomForest/kNN use the full 25350-row training set); this may understate SVM's achievable accuracy but doesn't invalidate the comparison's direction. Latency is single-sample CPU inference on the development machine, excludes MediaPipe detection time.

feature_ablation.caveat: Held-out stratified 80/20 split, same split as section 6/7.

resolution_confound_hypothesis._evidence: HYPOTHESIS (untested; the two tests that WERE run this pass -- confidence-control and hand-swap -- were both refuted, leaving resolution/framing as the most concrete remaining lead for A, E, F)
resolution_confound_hypothesis.statement: Image-resolution/framing heterogeneity (see dataset.image_resolution_heterogeneity) is a plausible contributing cause for the A/E/F cross-domain failures left unexplained by handedness composition, hand-slot assignment, detection-confidence, and hand-column-swap (all now directly tested). NOT experimentally isolated -- no controlled re-detection-at-matched-resolution test was run; would require access to original webcam video frames, which were never saved (only derived feature vectors).

isl_linguistic_validity.statement: A handful of Kaggle images (A, J, G, I) were visually spot-checked and show plausible ISL fingerspelling shapes; no certified ISL interpreter or Deaf community member has reviewed the vocabulary or images at any point in this project. Not a linguistic validation.

future_work_signer_session_disjoint_eval.statement: No signer- or session-disjoint evaluation exists or can exist without new, real multi-signer data collection. Protocol fully specified in docs/data_collection_protocol.md but NOT executed -- zero signer-disjoint data exists.

claims_paper_can_make: A real, CI-bounded, McNemar-significant cross-source accuracy gap exists (99.9% in-domain vs 28-50% cross-domain).
The gap holds across 4 different classifier families (RandomForest, kNN, SVM-RBF, MLP), not just one -- cross-domain accuracy ranges 42-51% for all four despite ~99%+ in-domain accuracy for all four.
The gap is not explained by webcam sample size (H1, refuted with a matched-size control).
The gap is not explained by the MediaPipe detection-confidence threshold mismatch (v2 controlled re-extraction, refuted).
The gap is not explained by a systematic right/left hand-column swap between pipelines (v2 hand-swap test, refuted).

Part of the gap is explained by a hand-to-feature-slot assignment mismatch between capture pipelines (J, K [partially], U, C), and a proposed fix significantly (CI- and McNemar-confirmed, seed-robust) improves it without in-domain cost.
Class K's failure is substantially explained by a near-total hand-count mismatch between sources (94.7% two-handed in Kaggle vs 100% one-handed in webcam), visually confirmed.
burst_id leakage is real for the legacy-webcam subset (macro-F1 0.999->0.895) but not a meaningful control for the Kaggle-dominated majority of current data.
Handedness has no measurable effect on within-domain accuracy; left-hand information is not redundant.

A and E and F remain genuinely unexplained after five directly-tested candidate causes (sample size, confidence threshold, hand-slot mismatch, hand-proximity, hand-column swap) -- an honestly-scoped open question, with image-resolution/framing heterogeneity as the most concrete untested lead.
claims_paper_must_not_make: Signer-independent or session-independent recognition -- no real multi-signer data exists.
That the cross-source gap is fully explained or fully fixed.
That the Kaggle vocabulary/images have been linguistically verified as authentic ISL.
That isl_dataset.csv currently supports 35 classes (it supports 31).
Anything from the current paper/main.tex draft, which describes a superseded 842-row/18-class snapshot.
That detection-threshold differences between pipelines explain any of the cross-source gap -- this was directly tested and refuted, not just left as an unquantified confound.
That One-Euro temporal filtering (webcam-only) was controlled for -- it was not, and cannot be without new data collection (raw unfiltered webcam frames were never saved).
That the hand-column-swap/mirroring-convention hypothesis explains the residual failures -- directly tested and refuted.
paper_main_tex_status: STALE -- describes the pre-Kaggle-merge 842-row/18-class dataset; central claim (burst-level leakage) is directly contradicted by current results. See PROJECT_DOSSIER_FINAL_V2.md section 7 for the recommended new structure.
